text:
tess: Quick RFC follow-up — I want to propose we drastically simplify the lease surface for prefix caching so correctness proofs and tests are smaller. TL;DR: decompose into three primitives (ClaimLease, ReleaseLease, QueryResidency) and push most tie-breaking into a small controller with optional best-effort persistence. Thoughts? @raj @elaine

raj: Sounds promising. Main worry: races when Claim arrives while Release is in-flight or after owner restart. How do we guarantee at-most-one owner without heavy consensus?

tess: Good call. My sketch: ClaimLease returns a (token, epoch) pair. Release requires that token. Epoch is monotonic per-prefix. If a restart happens, the old token is considered stale by controller once epoch increments. We avoid synchronous global consensus for every claim by using the controller as the tie-breaker — it can be eventual and best-effort, but Claim uses CAS semantics against epoch.

elaine: Persisting epochs in controller helps correctness but is CP-ish. Can we avoid sync persistence on every Claim? Maybe write through only on epoch bump; normal renewals are in-memory+heartbeat. That keeps fast path cheap.

sam: Also think about observability. We need metrics like lease_acquire_latency_ms, lease_conflicts_total, lease_token_expiration_count. And a debug endpoint for current leases for ops.

raj: For eviction semantics: evict path must consult QueryResidency(version) and compare returned epoch/token. If token mismatch (owner changed) abort eviction and requeue. That prevents double-evict or races where owner still expects residency.

tess: Proto sketch below (very small):

```proto
service LeaseManager {
  rpc ClaimLease(ClaimReq) returns (ClaimResp);
  rpc ReleaseLease(ReleaseReq) returns (ReleaseResp);
  rpc QueryResidency(QueryReq) returns (QueryResp);
}
message ClaimResp { string token = 1; int64 epoch = 2; bool granted = 3; }
```

elaine: We also need token GC. TTL? If heartbeats are every 10s we could set token TTL = 30s by default and make eviction conservative (soft-evict after 2xTTL).

tess: Plan was heartbeat 10s, TTL 30s, soft-evict threshold = 60s (2xTTL). If Claim fails because epoch mismatch, client should backoff with jitter and re-query residency.

sam: Ops checklist: CLI `rwd lease inspect <prefix>`, a /debug HTTP table, and a small canary plan (1% prefixes on staging, then 5% prod shard). Also add test harness that simulates kill-and-claim races.

raj: One more: fairness under thundering herd. Keep a tiny in-process FIFO queue of pending claimers per prefix so we don't thump the controller. The queue can be best-effort and approximate.

tess: Action items: (1) prototype the Claim/Release/Query API in runtime branch (no controller persistence first), (2) add metrics + inspect endpoint, (3) write unit+chaos tests for claim/release races, (4) canary on staging then single prod shard. I'll open a PR today. :thumbsup:

elaine: +1 on the plan. Please add a test case: owner dies immediately after ClaimResp but before heartbeat — ensure new claimant wins only after token TTL.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary scheduled for staging at 2025-03-05 18:00 UTC.
